scams.name: The Nagarekawa-Shintenchi Hustler Shakedown
scams.description: Hustlers in suits approach tourists in Hiroshima's entertainment district offering nightlife venues. Once inside, establishments with no visible pricing charge exorbitant amounts—one 2023 case involved a ¥830,000 charge. A 2019 police operation disbanded a 20-person hustler network delivering 281 customers in a single night.
scams.avoidance: Never follow hustlers anywhere in Nagarekawa, Yakkenbori, or Shintenchi. Avoid free information centers designed to steer customers to commission-paying venues. Research bars on Google Maps or Tabelog before arrival (4.3+ rating, 50+ reviews). Walk out immediately if no printed menu with prices is available. Call 110 if pressured.
scams.location: Nagarekawa and Shintenchi entertainment district, Naka-ku

scams.name: The Okonomiyaki Tourist Overcharge
scams.description: You order a single Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki at a restaurant in Shintenchi — the menu on the wall says ¥1,200. The pancake arrives, is excellent, and twenty minutes later the handwritten bill is ¥1,700. When you point at the menu, the server 'explains' that the ¥1,200 was for the basic version and you got the deluxe, or that prices went up last week and the wall hasn't been updated. A December 2024 TripAdvisor case documented a party of four billed ¥4,000 on an order that totaled ¥3,300 on the menu, with the receipt itself altered in pen.
scams.avoidance: Photograph the wall menu with your phone before you order — a timestamped photo ends the dispute on the spot. When the bill arrives, ask for a 'meisaisho' (明細書 — itemized receipt); if staff refuse or stall, pay only the menu price and leave. Stick to named okonomiyaki houses in Okonomimura (Reichan and Hassho both sit on the 4-star line with 500+ Japanese reviews); drift into no-name shops in side streets only if the posted menu looks complete and prices are visible from the sidewalk.
scams.location: Central Hiroshima okonomiyaki venues—Otemachi, Okonomimura, Shintenchi

scams.name: The Miyajima Deer Food-Grab Attack
scams.description: Miyajima deer, banned from commercial feeding since the 2010s, have become aggressive toward tourists carrying food or bags. Documentation includes gorings, kicks, and bites. A 4.96 million visitor count in 2025 increased confrontations, with incidents ranging from bites while eating ice cream to sustained chasing.
scams.avoidance: Finish any food before boarding the ferry or eat only inside restaurants. Carry food in opaque backpacks or zipped bags, never plastic convenience bags. Do not feed deer or touch them for photos. If charged, drop the bag item and walk away briskly without running or pushing.
scams.location: Miyajima ferry landing, Omotesando shopping street, Itsukushima Shrine approach

scams.name: The Miyajima Restaurant Card-Retry Triple Charge
scams.description: Restaurant servers claim card transactions failed and request multiple retry attempts. All attempts actually process successfully, resulting in triple-charging. A November 2024 incident at Niwa Cafe Miyama saw three charges approved despite claims of failure, with the restaurant unresponsive to refund requests.
scams.avoidance: Request to see every receipt (declined and approved) before leaving. Check your banking app in real time before retrying failed transactions. Pay cash where possible on Miyajima. Photograph terminal screens as evidence. Dispute with your bank immediately via chargeback rather than relying on merchant refunds.
scams.location: Miyajima restaurants along Omotesando approach and Omiyamae area

scams.name: The Miyajima Omotesando Souvenir Markup
scams.description: You step off the Miyajima ferry and walk into the first shop on Omotesando — the 300-meter shopping street between the pier and Itsukushima Shrine. A box of ten momiji manju (maple-leaf-shaped cakes) is ¥1,400. The exact same box at Nishiki-do in Hiroshima Station is ¥1,050 — a 33% premium for walking through the door. Further along the street, shops label factory-wrapped manju 'handmade Miyajima specialty' with no visible on-site production. The contents of the boxes are identical.
scams.avoidance: Buy your momiji manju at Hiroshima Station before you board the ferry — Nishiki-do and Fujii-ya both have booths at the shinkansen exit, and both stock the same brands the island sells. If you want to buy on the island anyway, walk past the first 200 meters of Omotesando (where premiums concentrate) before spending anything over ¥1,000, and only buy from shops where you can see a cook actually making manju in the window — Momiji-do and Iwamura have real on-site production.
scams.location: Miyajima Omotesando shopping street and ferry-terminal shops, Hatsukaichi
